comment: The vectors pinning Prima.LocusBackends, the backends wire between CYFR's programs controller and the backends service Locus serves; apps/prima/test/prima/locus_backends_test.exs consumes every section, and every end of the wire (the Locus service, CYFR's client and the image probe) reproduces them. Every consumer derives the control, seal and owner keys from the service key over the label, reproduces each control message's and each session message's canonical string, MAC and header, reads each control and session body and its answer to its members and writes them back to the same bytes, opens the sealed environment for its owner and lifetime only, parses every accepted header, refuses every malformed one as its kind and every one at another version token (v2) as unknown_version, refuses every invalid message with the error named and answers it with the refusal named, refuses every header under auth_rejected at its instant with its reason, and masks the input to the output. Integers are decimal in canonical strings and headers, and a header names its body's hex SHA-256 as body=, which an accepted header parses to as its body_hash. reserved_env_prefixes is Prima.KeeperProtocol's list, which the wire reserves. The fences are the service's, against state the wire does not hold: every fence_rejected vector runs against a fresh service at the boot the control vectors name, under the service key, each message presented at its now, with its headers beside its signature, and answered at its status until the refused one, which is the held message if one is held (its head sent and its body sent only once every later message is answered), else the last; it is refused with the code named, its body unread where read_body is false. advance_ms moves the service's lease clock; given names the pool its launcher answers ("unavailable" for none, 64 free uids otherwise), the live nonces the owner's cache already holds, and the stderr each program's process writes as it starts, which an open starts. The auth_rejected vectors are the envelope's alone: their bodies are bytes a signature covers, read as no message. The accepted sync's program names `hosts`, which every consumer reads back. A program may name `hosts`, the only hosts its processes reach beside the resolver and the deployment's private hosts, under Prima.KeeperProtocol's rule (1 to max_hosts distinct exact hostnames: the hosts_ vectors are refused); an open whose hosts resolve to no address is refused hosts_unresolved, and one the island's guard does not hold to them guard_unavailable. A hello and a status answer carry the box's memory{budget_bytes, admission_limit_bytes, held_bytes}, and a sync may carry athanor_memory_bytes, a positive count of bytes (the *_athanor_memory vectors are refused): the ceiling of the owner's athanor on the bounds its sessions on the box hold. given's memory_budget is the service's memory budget B with an overcommit of 1 (absent, room for every session the vector opens), under which the capacity_memory vector's second open, each at the default 512 MiB bound, is refused by memory alone while the pool has room. A session is opened in mode run, whose lines the run vectors (open, send, recv) carry, or in mode terminal (open_terminal, naming rows and cols, each 1 to bounds.max_pty_size; input, output and resize), whose bytes travel as standard base64 with padding both ways, an input of 1 to bounds.max_chunk_bytes bytes, and whose output is buffered in chunks of at most that many: every consumer signs, reads and writes the terminal vectors back as the run's, and a message of one mode to a session of the other is refused bad_request. A run's lines are masked one by one (masking); a terminal's output is masked as a stream (masking_stream): each chunk in turn releases what released names, the end of a chunk that begins a secret held until later bytes settle it, and what is held when the output ends is end.
